long_biography.plain_text:
Shamsuddin Abdul Kadir was the son of a chauffeur and a mother who could not read or write. His family shared a single rented room, and the Japanese occupation cost him several years of schooling. His father’s insistence on education led to an engineering scholarship in Brighton, followed by a career at Jabatan Telekom Malaysia.

In 1975, Shamsuddin left established employment to build a telecommunications systems company around Malaysian engineering capability. Sapura expanded into technology and other sectors, and his acquisition of an Australian coil-spring business created the automotive-components operation now known as Sapura Industrial. He chaired that company for five decades before retiring from its board in 2025.
